observable_outcome: One empty, owner-provided Google Cloud project holds the control plane, applied from a plan artifact a human approved before the apply ran and recorded in a committed preflight record: drift detection is clean, IAP refuses an unauthenticated request while an owner reaches /healthz, the Firestore default database and exactly the two declared composite indexes exist, no Cloud Scheduler job exists, Cloud Monitoring shows zero instances and zero billable instance time across a 20-minute idle window, the observed Firestore operation counts stay inside 50 percent of the free daily allowance and are not greater than the plane's own quota accounting, an image-digest rollback returns all traffic to the previous revision with canonical data unchanged, and the live evidence is registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with make check green at the committed checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Human approval precedes every side effect, mechanically. Before the first apply, .agents/v2/preflight/V2-014-gcp-apply.json is committed and pushed, valid against contracts/schemas/deployment-preflight.json, naming the target project, installation id, region, service name, image digest and the sha256 of the exact plan artifact to be applied, the seven required ceilings with fail_closed true, the rollback trigger, argv and completion conditions, the read-only verification argv, and an approval object whose approver is the owner, whose approved_at precedes the apply, and whose approval_reference names where the human recorded the approval. The apply applies that plan file and nothing else; if the plan is regenerated for any reason, its digest differs and a new approval is required before applying. The live evidence carries an artifact_refs entry with artifact_id deployment-preflight whose sha256 equals the committed record, so devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts fails if any live evidence exists without a prior approved record.

A2. Before anything else, re-observe the external preconditions. If the project, billing approval, Artifact Registry image, state bucket, IAP brand, owner allowlist or workload-identity provider is missing, produce no evidence at all, make no cloud call, and report to Sol the exact string 'external-unavailable: gcp-project; needs: empty org-attached project id and region, billing account with an approved zero-cost ceiling and budget alerts, pre-created Artifact Registry repository with the pushed image digest, private versioned OpenTofu state bucket, IAP brand with owner emails and origins, and a workload identity provider plus deploy service account distributed only as GitHub secrets with no key file' together with next_owner sol. Do not write the task-state file yourself and do not register any local or emulator result as a live substitute.

A3. Clean-project confirmation. Every emptiness condition of dp-v2-012 d1 is observed read-only and recorded as a verification entry in the preflight record with the argv actually executed: lifecycleState ACTIVE, zero Cloud Run services, no Firestore database including no (default), zero composite indexes, zero Cloud Scheduler jobs, no non-default service account, no IAM member matching agentic-loop-*, and an OpenTofu state listing no resources. State in the report that this project can never be returned to this state by OpenTofu, because prevent_destroy and deletion_policy ABANDON keep the Firestore database alive, so a second clean-project exercise needs a new project.

A4. Apply. The five ordered steps of dp-v2-012 d3 run in order with their argv recorded: infra-policy, infra-plan producing infra/build/infra.tfplan, tofu show -json producing the plan JSON and its sha256, the recorded human approval, then cd infra && tofu apply -input=false build/infra.tfplan. enable_reconcile_scheduler is false and reconcile_cost_preflight_approved is false in the applied tfvars, which lives outside the repository and is never committed. The applied plan JSON contains no google_cloud_scheduler_job resource and creates no resource outside infra/.

A5. Verify, all read-only and all recorded with the argv actually executed: tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode exits 0; the Cloud Run service reports min instances 0, max instances 1, concurrency 1, cpu 0.08, memory 512Mi, cpu_idle true, iap_enabled true and the digest-pinned image; an unauthenticated request to the service URI returns 302 or 403 and never 200; an owner request through IAP returns 200 from /healthz; the (default) Firestore database is FIRESTORE_NATIVE in the configured location and exactly the two composite indexes of infra/indexes.tf exist; and zero Cloud Scheduler jobs exist.

A6. Scale-to-zero. Across a continuous 20-minute window with no request and no reconcile trigger, Cloud Monitoring reports run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count aggregated MAX equal to 0 for both state=active and state=idle, and run.googleapis.com/container/billable_instance_time summed equal to 0. Record the window start and end, the metric names and the argv actually used; if a different observable or CLI surface is substituted, record what was substituted and why, and never present the configured min_instance_count as the observation.

A7. Budget guard, live. For the UTC day of the exercise, the observed Firestore read, write and delete counts from Cloud Monitoring are at or below 25,000, 10,000 and 10,000, and are not greater than the totals in the plane's own daily quota document, which proves the reservation is conservative in the correct direction rather than merely present. Observed stored bytes are at or below 536,870,912. Cloud Run billable instance time and request count for the month are at or below 360,000 instance-seconds and 1,000,000 requests. If any ceiling is reached, stop, record it as an explicit capacity-exhaustion outcome, and do not continue by raising a ceiling.

A8. Rollback. With the service serving the current digest, set image_digest back to the previous known-good 64-hex digest, re-plan, obtain and commit a new approval for the new plan digest, and apply the new saved plan. Rollback is complete only when all four conditions hold and are recorded: 100 percent of traffic is served by the revision built from the previous digest, tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode exits 0, /healthz returns 200 through IAP, and a sampled read of canonical Firestore documents has the same content digest as before the rollback. tofu destroy is never attempted and tofu state rm is never used.

A9. Exactly one evidence record, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-014-gcp-live-apply.json, is created with task_id V2-014, id ev-v2-014-gcp-live-apply, component gcp-live-apply and result passed, one check per acceptance item above with the argv actually executed and an observed_at, plus the artifact_refs entry of A1. Its evidence_key is the sha256 of the project reference, image digest and plan digest joined by newlines, so the key is reproducible from the live target. It is registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with an evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the file, and devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green: registered in the index and the ledger test green is the completion definition, not 'the checks passed'.

A10. No access token, session, service-account key, tfvars file or tfstate file enters the repository, the evidence, the preflight record, the runbook or any log excerpt. Project id, region, service name, image digest and plan digest are the only target identifiers recorded.

A11. docs/operations/gcp-runbook.md records the observed facts and their observation date: the pricing figures re-confirmed at execution time, the exact apply and rollback argv used, the metric names used for the scale-to-zero and budget observations, and the fact that a second clean-project apply requires a new project. No other tracked document is modified.

A12. After committing the evidence, devbox run --pure -- make check is green on the committed state, including secrets, because gitleaks git scans committed history and the preflight record contains 64-hex digests. Checkpoints are pushed one at a time and the parent commit's v2 selective CI is confirmed green before the next push.
constraints: No side effect before the approved preflight record is committed. An apply whose plan digest does not match the approved record is a failure, not a retry.

Stay inside the approved ceilings of dp-v2-012 d2. Create no resource that infra/ does not declare, and create nothing that costs money outside the approved list, including no load balancer, no named Firestore database, no Artifact Registry repository and no Cloud Scheduler job.
Never run tofu destroy, never run tofu state rm, and never bypass prevent_destroy or deletion_protection. Emergency deletion is a separate approval with its own state backup and impact record.
Never weaken IAP: do not add unauthenticated invoker access, do not widen ingress, and do not replace the IAP assertion with a caller-controlled header.
Record the argv actually executed. If a CLI or metric surface differs from the design, record the substitution; never restate the assumed command as if it had run.

Do not modify any code, script, schema or workflow. If the live exercise reveals a defect in infra/, scripts/ or the application, stop and escalate: that repair belongs to a V2-013-scoped follow-up, not to this task.
Do not add gcloud or any package to devbox.json or devbox.lock; use curl against the documented REST surfaces with a short-lived federated token.
Do not write any task-state file. Report block_reason and status changes to Sol, who owns every transition.

If the project cannot host an IAP brand because it is outside an organization or Cloud Identity, stop and escalate to product_orchestrator; direct IAP is a deployment invariant and must not be substituted.
If any observation cannot be made read-only, or if a verification would itself create a billable resource, stop and escalate rather than improvising a mutation.
Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree. Push checkpoints one at a time and wait for the parent commit CI to be green.
Japanese for the tracked documents; English identifiers in records and configuration.
